Good video, but you have the physics slightly mixed up. Lower frequencies have longer wavelengths, so they actually travel much farther and penetrate walls/glass far better. AM radio (~1 MHz) travels way farther than FM (~100 MHz) for this exact reason, but FM penetrates walls better.
That's why SpaceX using mid-band (~2 GHz) and low-band (like 800 MHz) spectrum is so crucial for Direct-to-Cell.  Those lower frequencies reach standard phones outdoors and penetrate foliage/glass much better than their existing high-frequency 70–90 GHz feeder links ever could.
Low-band signals like 800 MHz actually travel very well up to satellites, but having ground hardware—like Starlink dishes on homes, Superchargers, and Robotaxis—acting as local relays and mobile towers creates a super resilient mesh network.

Good video, but you have the physics slightly mixed up. Lower frequencies have longer wavelengths, so they actually travel much farther and penetrate walls/glass far better. AM radio (~1 MHz) travels way farther than FM (~100 MHz) for this exact reason, but FM penetrates walls better.
That's why SpaceX using mid-band (~2 GHz) and low-band (like 800 MHz) spectrum is so crucial for Direct-to-Cell.  Those lower frequencies reach standard phones outdoors and penetrate foliage/glass much better than their existing high-frequency 70–90 GHz feeder links ever could.
Low-band signals like 800 MHz actually travel very well up to satellites, but having ground hardware—like Starlink dishes on homes, Superchargers, and Robotaxis—acting as local relays and mobile towers creates a super resilient mesh network.
